## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Bhojanadāyakattheraapadāna* is a biographical poem preserved within the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. As designated by its title, the text recounts the past karmic merit and spiritual attainment of an elder (*thera*) associated with the donation of food (*bhojana*) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

No curated cross-canonical parallels are identified for this text on SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus finds no cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan literature meeting the significance threshold [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus documents 69 matching passages across 28 Pali texts, illustrating the formulaic nature of verse composition in late canonical and commentarial literature [DharmaNexus]. The largest share of text reuse occurs with the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, 7 matches, sharing segments §4.2–5.3) [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Therāpadāna* itself, prominent textual overlaps occur with the *Bhājanapālakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 234, sharing segments §4.3–8.1), the *Abbhañjanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 276, sharing segments §4.2–8.1), the *Tālavaṇṭadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 219), and the *Sayanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 49) [DharmaNexus].
